readme.orgIntro: The export contains all data for {who} in TimeTrack, retrieved {date} (Danish time).
readme.orgDataJson:
data.json
  All tables in one file, complete and machine-readable. Use it if the
  data needs to move to another system. Times are in UTC (ISO 8601).
readme.csv:
csv/
  One file per table, for Excel, Numbers or Google Sheets. Semicolon as
  separator, UTF-8, times in Danish time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS),
  decimals with a comma and Ja/Nej (yes/no) for true/false. Fields with lists
  or lookups appear as JSON in the cell. The columns have the same names as in data.json.
readme.orgFiles:
filer/
  Files attached to tasks, attachments from emails and logos.
  Images and links written into text (notes, descriptions and comments)
  have not been retrieved. The address is still in the text.
readme.orgFilesCount: Number of files in the export: {count}.{extra}
readme.filesMissing: Number of files not included: {count}. They are listed in filer/oversigt.csv with the reason.
readme.orgFilesTail:
filer/oversigt.csv shows where each file came from and where it is in
  the export. An attachment stored in the database is replaced by the path
  to the file ("filIEksporten") in data.json and CSV.
readme.orgRelations:
How the tables fit together
---------------------------
Every row has an id. Columns ending in Id (e.g. clientId, projectId,
userId) point to an id in another table. The users' names and emails are in
brugere.csv. Clients are in kunder.csv, projects in projekter.csv.
readme.excludedHeading:
What is not included, and why
-----------------------------
readme.redacted:
Access keys and secrets have been removed because they must not be usable
outside TimeTrack. This applies to these columns, where they exist:
readme.orgOtherOrgs: Data that the users have in other organisations in TimeTrack is not included.
readme.orgRetention:
Storage
-------
The link to the export works for 7 days. After that the ZIP file is deleted
from TimeTrack's storage. The file is not encrypted, so keep it somewhere
safe: it contains personal data about employees and clients.
readme.userIntro: The export contains the data that belongs to you {where} in TimeTrack, retrieved {date} (Danish time). It is for you as a user, so you can see what is stored about you and take it with you (GDPR articles 15 and 20).
readme.userDataJson:
data.json
  Your data in one file, complete and machine-readable. Times are in
  UTC (ISO 8601).
readme.userFiles:
filer/
  Attachments stored in the database and images you attached to tasks
  in the organisation. Images and links written into text
  (notes, descriptions and comments) have not been retrieved.
readme.userRelations:
How the tables fit together
---------------------------
Every row has an id. Columns ending in Id (e.g. clientId, projectId)
point to an id in another table. The tables starting with reference-
contain only the id and name of the clients, projects, tasks and other items
that your own rows point to, so you can read them without the rest of
the organisation's information.
readme.userOwnOnly:
The export only has rows that belong to you. Colleagues' data is not included.
It only covers the organisation you ordered it in, because each
organisation is the controller of its own data. If you are a member of several,
switch to the other organisation in TimeTrack and order a new
export there.
readme.userAdminOnly:
Hourly rates, amounts and cost prices are only included if you are an owner or
administrator. They are the organisation's business data and not your
personal data.
readme.userExcludedGroups: These groups of data are not included:
readme.userRetention:
Storage
-------
The link to the export works for 7 days, and only for you when you are signed in.
After that the ZIP file is deleted from TimeTrack's storage. The file is not
encrypted, so keep it somewhere safe: it contains your personal data.

readme.statusTooBig: Not included: the file is over 50 MB
readme.jobStalled: The export stalled. Order a new one.
readme.notMemberAnymore: You are no longer a member of the organisation.
readme.notOwnerAnymore: You are no longer an owner or administrator of the organisation.
readme.storageMissing: The export storage is not set up, so the export cannot be saved.

readme.accessNotMember: You are no longer a member of the organisation

userExclusionGroups.shared: Clients, projects, invoices, prepaid packages, templates and other setup that the organisation owns and shares. They belong to the organisation and not to you, even if you created them. Ask the owner or an administrator.
userExclusionGroups.config: The organisation's own setup: departments, public holidays, absence types, permissions, modules and the like. Ask the owner or an administrator.
userExclusionGroups.thirdParty: Tables with content from and about other people, e.g. emails, report recipients, invitations and client portal users. TimeTrack must not pass these on without the others' consent.
userExclusionGroups.login: Sign-in and devices: sessions, passwords, passkeys, keys for the API, browser extension and push. They contain secrets that must not be usable outside TimeTrack. You can see and end your active sessions under Settings > Security.
userExclusionGroups.timetrack: Data for which TimeTrack itself is the controller: subscription, support, feedback, product statistics and internal notes. Write to timetrack@timetrack.dk if you want them.
